optimizationCandidatesExamined.whyInteresting: The only item on the e2e critical path that lives in editable repo surface rather than .github/workflows. Step median 7s of a 167s job.
optimizationCandidatesExamined.evidence: Extracted the walker verbatim (it only touches plain ESTree objects, so it runs without espree) and timed it on synthetic left-nested '&&' chains — the shape minified bundles are full of. Scaling is ~4x per doubling of N: 27ms@500, 126ms@1000, 457ms@2000, 1867ms@4000, 7595ms@8000. Cause: for every LogicalExpression, typeofNamesIn(node.left) re-walks the entire left subtree, so a left-nested chain of depth N costs O(N^2).
optimizationCandidatesExamined.fixAttempted: Memoize the typeof-name set per node in one post-order pass, sharing the set object with the only non-empty child and copying only when two non-empty sets merge.
optimizationCandidatesExamined.result: REJECTED — trades one quadratic for another. 783x faster on deep left-nested chains (7595ms -> 9.7ms at N=8000) but 55x SLOWER on flat guard-then-use statement lists (16.9ms -> 923ms at N=8000), because N siblings with distinct non-empty sets force N successive set copies at the parent. Output verified identical in both shapes, so the rejection is purely on performance.
optimizationCandidatesExamined.doNotRepeat: Do not re-propose naive per-node set memoization here. A real fix needs a structure that is cheap for BOTH shapes (persistent/immutable sets, or indexing only the nodes that are actually queried) — and it cannot be verified in this sandbox anyway (see blocker).
optimizationCandidatesExamined.blocker: No node_modules and no pnpm/turbo in the sandbox, so espree/eslint-scope/globals do not resolve and the scanner cannot be run end-to-end. The 7s -> ? CI wall-clock effect is unmeasurable here even for a correct fix.
optimizationCandidatesExamined.upside: Even a perfect fix is ~7s of a 167s job (~4%). Worth doing for its own sake; not a headline.

structuralWasteReportOnly.turboPnpmCacheReservationRaces: Still present and now observed on BOTH shards in the same week: 'Failed to save: Unable to reserve cache with key ...' on worker 09-30 (node-cache pnpm key), web 09-29 (5 separate turbo keys), web 10-01 (node-cache + pnpm-lockfile-verified), web 10-02 (2 turbo keys). Concurrent matrix jobs race for identical cache keys; the loser silently discards its upload. Costs no wall time directly but wastes the upload and degrades later hit rates.
structuralWasteReportOnly.runnerQueueOutliers: BLACKSMITH_RUNNER_MESSAGE_WAIT_MS in sampled shards: 109, 113, 205, 261, 284, 599. Mostly sub-300ms; the 599ms on the 09-30 worker lines up with that day being the slowest. One run (36872085195, 10-01) had a 58s runner wait, the only large one in 29 runs.
